close_reason:
tasks-client's with_tasks_session changed from fn(self, Session) to fn(&self, Session), with impl cloning self. Matches the canonical extension-client template established by jmap-mail-client::JmapMailExt::with_mail_session and the 6 other sibling extension clients (chat, calendars, contacts, filenode, sharing, metadata).

A caller using multiple extension clients in the same workflow no longer has to clone the JmapClient before calling with_tasks_session — the compiler now enforces uniform behavior across all 8 extension clients. Pre-1.0 v0.1.x — small breaking change for the one outlier.

Workspace cargo test, clippy, rustdoc all clean.
description:
**Files**: crate-jmap-tasks-client/src/lib.rs:62, :66

**Divergence**:
- mail-client, chat-client, calendars-client, contacts-client, filenode-client, sharing-client, metadata-client — all 7 define:
    fn with_<x>_session(&self, session: jmap_base_client::Session) -> methods::SessionClient
- tasks-client (crate-jmap-tasks-client/src/lib.rs:62 declaration, :66 impl) instead defines:
    fn with_tasks_session(self, session: jmap_base_client::Session) -> methods::SessionClient
  (consumes the receiver — implementation uses \`client: self\`, not \`client: self.clone()\`)

**What goes wrong**: any caller that needs to use multiple extension clients (e.g. a mail + tasks workflow) must clone the JmapClient before calling with_tasks_session, but does NOT need to for any of the other 7 extensions. The compiler does not enforce this asymmetry — the call site only fails the second time the caller tries to use the moved client. A user reading the canonical mail-client example and pattern-matching to tasks will produce a compile-error stack that looks like 'value moved here in previous call'.

**Fix**: tasks-client should take \`&self\` to match the 7-crate canonical shape. The impl change is \`fn with_tasks_session(&self, ...) { ... client: self.clone() ... }\` mirroring the canonical mail-client at crate-jmap-mail-client/src/lib.rs:86.
title: tasks-client `with_tasks_session(self, ...)` consumes the client while 7 sibling extension clients take `&self`
